full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Abdur Rashid, J.: This Rule was obtained by the defendants against judgment and decree dated 31.08.2000 passed by Subordinate Judge, 1st Court at Bogra in Other Class Appeal No. 58 of 2000 affirming those dated 29.03.2000 passed by Assistant Judge (In-Charge) at Gabtali in Bogra in Other Class Suit No. 131 of 1999. 

 5. Trial Court decreed the suit and clock-wed that the appointment of defendant No. 4 void and by way of a mandatory injunction directed the defendant No. 3 to appoint the plaintiff in her place within 30 days as prayed for. On appeal therefrom the Court of appeal below dismissed the same and affirmed the decree of the Trial Court by the impugned judgment and decree. 

 6. Mr. Shahidul Islam for the petitioners submits that in the facts and circumstances of the case and pursuant to the circular of the Education Board the managing committee of a non-government school having exercised its discretion in the matter of appointment of a teacher, the Court of appeal below erred in law in affirming the decree of the trial court which has resulted in failure of justice. Secondly, he submits that by securing the top position amongst the candidates, even if conceded for the sake of argument, the plaintiff acquired no right within the meaning of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act for getting a declaration, and/or mandatory injunction for appointment under Section 55 of the Act. Lastly, he submits that both the Courts below erred in law in decreeing the suit on misreading exhibit Kha and Kha(1) and the circular dated 14.01.98. 

 7. Mr. Asaduzzaman, on the other hand, opposes the Rule mainly on the ground that when the plaintiff secured the first position amongst the candidates the managing committee of the school having failed to appoint such competent candidate in the absence of any good reason, such decision of the managing committee was rightly struck down by the trial Court and correctly affirmed by the appellate court by the impugned judgment and decree which have occasioned no failure of justice. 

 In the State Medical Faculty V Kshiti Bhusan, AIR 1961 Calcutta 31, a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court set aside a decree by which the plaintiff was declared to be entitled to a certificate of the State Medical Faculty of West Bengal to practice Western Medical Science, and defendants do grant the plaintiff a certificate. 

 15. Under Section 42 of the Act, one entitled to any legal character may institute a suit against any person denying or interested to deny his title to such character or right and the Court may in its discretion make a declaration that he is so entitled. First position, even if accepted to have been secured by the plaintiff, in the test for appointment has not clothed him with any such legal right within the meaning of Section 42. Similarly, for a decree for mandatory injunction under Section 55 of the Act, there must be existence of a legal obligation on the part of the defendants to perform certain acts, and breach of such obligation must be based for the decree sought for in the suit. The obligation referred in the section is a legal obligation and not moral obligation. In holding the examination or viva voce for appointment of a teacher the defendants or more precisely the managing committee of the school did not take upon them any obligation to appoint the plaintiff in the school. 

 20. In view of the law as discussed above and in the tads and circumstances of the case the trial court wrongly exercised its jurisdiction in decreeing the suit and the court of appeal below has com-mitted serious error of law in affirming such decree of the trial court that has no doubt resulted in failure of justice. 

 21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. No costs. The impugned judgment and decree of the Court of appellate below affirming those of the trial court in decreeing the suit are hereby set aside. The suit is dismissed. The order of stay granted at the time of issue of the Rule is recalled and vacated.
